correctness.rationale: By signed rearrangement the support function is sum_j(2j-1)|u|_(j), and central symmetry doubles it for width. On a stratum with >=2 distinct positive magnitude levels, the restricted support is a positive linear functional on a sphere of block levels: nonstationary points descend and the only stationary point is a strict maximum on that stratum; hence no other minima. At a single positive level with support k, for tan(theta)<1/(2sqrt(k)) the perturbed positive coordinates stay above all formerly-zero absolute coordinates, so the width separates exactly into base width cos(theta) plus active block A_k(a)=sum_{i<j}|a_i-a_j| and inactive C_m(z)=sum_j(2j-1)|z|_(j). Zero-mean upper-step decomposition gives A_k(a)>=sqrt(k(k-1))||a|| (k>=2); nonnegative sorted upper-step decomposition gives C_m(z)>=min(2m-1,m sqrt(m))||z||. Pure one-coordinate-split or inactive indicator rays attain sharp slopes, and orthogonality forces the smaller term. Integer comparisons yield strict switch k<2m vs k>=2m for 2<=k<n without ties. In open signed Weyl chambers the support is linear and all local maxima are its normalized signed-weight gradients; zero/tie perturbations increase support to first order, excluding boundary maxima. Sharp global minimum is axes for n>=3 and equal full-support vectors for n=2. Independently verified squared step inequalities, attaining rays and switch for n<=29; universal classification uses the analytic step decomposition, not those finite checks.
